title: Turning Back Without Forgetting: Selective Backward Refinement for Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: A three-stage procedure selects which earlier modules benefit from a new task and refines them safely without interference.
layout: 3 colored stage panels left-to-right plus legend panel; OR gate between criteria
description: A left-to-right pipeline of three rounded, pastel panels with colored title tabs, followed by a legend column. S1 (blue, Initialization) shows frozen task blocks T1..T(t-1), their snowflake-marked prompts u1..u(t-1), a brace merging them into the prompt set P(t-1), and protected gradient subspaces below. S2 (green, Correlation Estimation) stacks two criteria boxes, update-level projection and response-level loss-distribution, with threshold inequalities marked by red crosses or teal checks and joined by an OR diamond. S3 (orange, Training) shows subset selection S_t within P(t-1), training a new prompt with flame icons, and a geometric inset of an allowed update orthogonal to a dotted protected-subspace ellipse. The legend on the right explains the notation and icons.
caption: Overview of the proposed SABER framework. (S1) the state after learning tasks T1, . . . , Tt−1, where task-specific prompts have been learned and frozen and their corresponding protected gradient subspaces are maintained; at this point, the model is now at task Tt and a new prompt ut is initialized for learning; (S2) task correlation estimation using either update-level criteria (projection and compatibility) or response-level criteria (loss-distribution) to select prior prompts; and (S3) training on task Tt, where ut is learned, and selected prior prompts are refined orthogonally to their protected subspaces, enabling positive backward transfer.
abstract: While prompt-based parameter-efficient continual learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting by isolating task-specific prompts, this isolation also limits later tasks from improving earlier ones, leaving backward knowledge transfer underexplored. We address this limitation by proposing Selective bAckward refinement for positive Backward knowledge transfER (SABER), a replay-free framework that enables controlled backward transfer in prompt-based continual learning. SABER determines when backward refinement is beneficial using complementary task-correlation criteria based on prompt-gradient geometry and loss-distribution similarity, and how to perform refinement safely by restricting updates to non-interfering directions in the prompt parameter space. Extensive experiments across multiple continual learning benchmarks and diverse pretrained backbones, including T5-Large, LLaMA, and Qwen, demonstrate that SABER consistently achieves positive backward transfer while maintaining strong overall average performance. Code is available at https://github.com/OptMN-Lab/SABER-ICML-2026/.
